tweet.text:
This is an interesting thought, but won't happen for a few structural reasons:

1) Most consumers are too busy to hunt for yield on their deposits.  They're busy driving to work.  Making lunches for their kids.  Cleaning.  Taking care of ailing parents.  Fighting medical bills.  Watching football.  Doing other activities.

2) Consumers who live paycheck to paycheck don't have big deposits to move.

3) Consumers with big deposits already optimize — either for yield or for tax savings.  So some of them are sitting in treasury funds through their wealth advisors vs. high yield savings accounts.
